item.title: 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary election of the party, was unlawfully substituted by Ribadu. Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary. However, he was later replaced by Ribadu. Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution. He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party. He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party. Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died. He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void. The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. (NAN) The post 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Vandalism, illegal connections threaten Kano water supply
item.description: Over 45 pipeline repairs completed, says commissioner By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — The Kano State Government has warned residents against vandalism, illegal connections and other activities capable of damaging public water infrastructure and disrupting the supply of drinking water across the state. The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, gave the warning at a press conference in Kano on Friday while briefing journalists on the progress of ongoing rehabilitation of water facilities and restoration of supply to communities. Hashim said the ministry had identified cases of unauthorised connections to water pipelines, vandalism, indiscriminate drilling around major water lines and improper handling of distribution valves. He added that some water pipes had also been damaged by construction activities, refuse burning and other activities around drainage channels. “We appeal to the general public to cooperate with the Ministry in protecting water infrastructure. Our assessment has identified cases of unauthorised tapping of pipelines, vandalism and damage to pipes crossing drainage channels,” he said. The commissioner urged residents, contractors and those executing construction, road and drainage projects to consult relevant authorities before embarking on activities that could affect water pipelines. He also called on residents to promptly report burst pipes, leakages, suspected vandalism and illegal connections to the appropriate authorities. According to him, the restoration of water supply has exposed weaknesses in some old pipelines, many of which had remained without regular water flow for several years. He explained that the return of water pressure to the distribution network had resulted in leakages and pipe bursts in some locations, necessitating urgent repairs and replacement of damaged infrastructure. Hashim disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 45 repair and replacement interventions across different parts of the metropolis. The affected areas include Goron Dutse, Jakara, Kofar Ruwa, Kurmi, Dukawa, Kofar Wambai, Fagge, Club Road, Tudun Wada, Gidan Zakka, Gabari, Koki, Mandawari and Sharada. He said the interventions involved replacing damaged asbestos-cement pipes, fixing leaking PVC pipelines, installing valves and repairing faulty connections. The commissioner further disclosed that water had been pumped from Challawa Water Works to the Goron Dutse reservoirs, which have a reported capacity of 42.5 million litres, before being released into the distribution network. He listed communities that had received water to include Goron Dutse, Gwammaja, Jakara, Kofar Mazugal, Muskwani, Kofar Wambai, Mandawari, Fagge, Tudun Wada, Gama, Kofar Ruwa and Alfindiki, among others. item.title: Tinubu Must Stay group set to unveil presidential library, reform observatory
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly known as Tinubu Must Stay, has announced plans to establish a National Reform Documentation and Impact Observatory, a public digital policy archive and a possible future presidential library for President Bola Tinubu. Chairman of the Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the group, Malam Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, disclosed this on Friday during the commissioning of its National Secretariat in Abuja. He said the records would start with Tinubu’s years as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, then cover policy developments under successive administrations, his national political career and his presidency from 2023. According to him, the archive would span public revenue administration, infrastructure, investment, education, economic management, digital transformation and institutional development. Students, researchers, historians, policymakers and ordinary citizens would be given access to original documents, implementation records, economic data and independent assessments. Inuwa said the library, the observatory and the archive remained long-term aspirations that would need feasibility studies, sustainable funding, proper governance and professional archival standards. “History serves future generations when it preserves evidence, not merely admiration,” he said. He added that the documentation must make room for achievements, implementation difficulties, independent criticism and lessons learned. The announcement came with a membership claim. Inuwa said the group, formally launched on October 1, 2026, had recorded 61,093 validated members within seven weeks across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). He said the group had representation in 730 of the country’s 774 local government areas, about 94 per cent geographical coverage. Its digital database also captures 4,750 wards and 22,584 polling units. Inuwa said 65 per cent of members, roughly 40,000 people, were aged between 18 and 34, while the membership was 65 per cent men and 35 per cent women. “The most remarkable feature of our membership is its youthful composition. This is not merely a demographic statistic. It places a profound responsibility upon our institution,” he said. He said young Nigerians needed more than a seat in political conversations, naming quality education, employable skills, technology, finance and markets as what would turn the country’s demographic potential into prosperity. To that end, the group would run grassroots entrepreneurship workshops, digital skills training, mentorship programmes and policy dialogues. “Today, we are not merely opening an office. We are opening a new chapter in our responsibility to Nigeria,” he said. Inuwa said the secretariat would serve as a centre for research, civic engagement, youth empowerment and the documentation of policies and institutions shaping national development. item.title: Nasarawa attracts $2.3bn investments in seven years — Abdullahi
item.description: Records 21 reforms, 11 PPP projects worth ₦93bn By John Alechenu ABUJA — Nasarawa State has attracted more than $2.3 billion in investments over the past seven years following reforms and institutional development aimed at making the state more competitive and investor-friendly. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency, Ibrahim Abdullahi, disclosed this at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. Abdullahi said the investments cut across agriculture, solid minerals, retail, commercial activities, manufacturing, agro-processing and education. He added that the state also implemented 11 public-private partnership (PPP) projects valued at about ₦93 billion within the period. According to him, the achievements were the outcome of seven years of reforms and deliberate institution-building under Governor Abdullahi Sule, rather than publicity campaigns or political slogans. Recounting the beginning of the process, Abdullahi said he was invited into the Nasarawa State public service seven years ago, when Governor Sule appointed him as economic adviser. He said the assignment was to develop the state’s investment profile and position it as an attractive destination for investors. He thanked the organisers of the forum for recognising Governor Sule with an honour presented a few days earlier. Abdullahi said one of the first lessons from the assignment was the need to establish the necessary structures before embarking on investment promotion. “So we could not go out and invite people to come to Nasarawa State without building any framework around it. That is to say that you cannot communicate something that is not there. You cannot communicate something that hasn’t been built. So, we put our heads down and began to build,” he said. He explained that the state’s vision, as contained in the Nasarawa Economic Development Strategy, was to make it one of Nigeria’s most competitive states through improved and accelerated economic growth that would translate into better living conditions for residents. Under the strategy, he said, the government implemented more than 21 reforms focused on improving the business environment and making the state attractive to investors. He said the reforms were designed to guarantee a conducive business climate, competitive returns on investment and improved general welfare for residents. According to him, the measures included the digitisation of revenue administration and improvements in the state’s fiscal and financial management framework. Abdullahi said the reforms provided the foundation for the state to confidently promote its investment opportunities to local and international investors. He noted that investors were attracted not by impressive speeches but by predictability, transparency, good returns and a government that honoured its commitments. item.title: MDGIF delivers 25 operational CNG stations nationwide
item.description: Fund backs 31 projects, as FG expands university initiative to 20 institutions By Uzoma Marvellous The Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF) has supported the delivery of 25 operational Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) stations across the country in two years, with its investment portfolio expanding to 31 projects comprising 205 infrastructure assets. The Executive Director of MDGIF, Mr Oluwole Adama, disclosed this during the commissioning of CNG refuelling facilities at the University of Lagos (UNILAG), University of Ibadan (UI), Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) and Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE) on Thursday. Adama said the achievements reflected the Federal Government’s efforts to deepen domestic gas utilisation, expand infrastructure and make natural gas more accessible to motorists and transport operators. “In just two years, MDGIF has supported the delivery of 25 fully operational CNG stations nationwide, bringing cleaner, more affordable fuel closer to motorists and transport operators,” he said. Established under Section 52 of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), the fund supports investments in midstream and downstream gas infrastructure. Adama disclosed that the UNILAG facility was the 11th CNG station being commissioned in Lagos State, adding that nine additional university stations, mostly in Northern Nigeria, would be commissioned within weeks. “Eleven stations in one state is a clear signal that CNG is no longer a promise for tomorrow. In Lagos, it is becoming part of everyday life,” he said. Meanwhile, the Federal Government is expanding its university CNG initiative to 20 institutions, with 11 stations already commissioned under the programme. The Chief Executive Officer of Femadec Energy Limited, Engr. Fola Akinnola, said the company planned to complete six additional stations before the end of 2026, while the remaining three would be commissioned early in 2027. The programme began with facilities at the University of Abuja, Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, and Federal University of Technology, Owerri. Four other facilities were subsequently commissioned at the University of Uyo, University of Calabar, Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun, and University of Nigeria, Enugu Campus. Akinnola said the 20-campus initiative was designed to reduce transportation costs for students, lecturers and other university employees while promoting cleaner energy adoption. “Campus communities are dynamic hubs of daily movement, where high transportation costs directly impact students, faculty and support staff alike. By systematically delivering this 20-campus network, we are providing immediate, practical relief—cutting campus transit fuel costs while significantly lowering carbon emissions,” he said. item.title: Nigeria to become world’s third-largest Muslim population by 2035 – Report
item.description: Nigeria is projected to have the world’s third-largest Muslim population by 2035, behind Pakistan and India, as Islam is expected to record significant growth globally over the next decade. The projection is contained in a report by the Pew Research Centre titled Future of World Religions, released on Wednesday. According to the report, Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians globally by 2070 if current demographic trends continue, marking a significant shift in the religious composition of the world. The report projects that the global Muslim population will exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, compared with just under three billion Christians. It attributed the projected growth largely to differences in fertility rates, noting that Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children between 2020 and 2025, compared with 2.5 for Christian women and 1.6 for women belonging to other religious groups. The report explained that a population requires an average of about 2.1 children per woman to maintain its size across generations. Under the projections, Pakistan will have the world’s largest Muslim population by 2035, followed by India, Nigeria and Indonesia, which currently has the largest Muslim population. The findings further indicated that four of the 10 countries with the largest Muslim populations by 2070 would be in Africa, namely Nigeria, Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan. The Pew Research Centre’s projections cover 201 countries and territories, accounting for 99.98 per cent of the world’s population. It said the estimates were based on the assumption that existing trends in fertility, mortality and religious switching would continue, while acknowledging that developments such as wars, natural disasters and economic changes could alter the projections. The report also projected significant changes in the global Christian population, particularly in the United States, which is expected to lose its Christian-majority status, although Christians would remain the country’s largest religious group. It further predicted that the Democratic Republic of the Congo would overtake the United States as the country with the largest Christian population. For centuries, Christianity has remained the world’s largest religion, but the latest projections point to a gradual shift in the global religious landscape, driven largely by population growth and demographic differences. item.title: Tinubu’s NYSC certificate: Court dismisses Atiku, ADC application
item.description: A Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) seeking to amend their suit challenging President Bola Tinubu’s eligibility for the 2027 presidential election over his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate. In a ruling on Friday, according to TheCable, Justice Inyang Ekwo held that the proposed amendments would introduce new facts and alter the substance of the original case. The judge upheld the arguments by Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) that the applicants were attempting to introduce a fresh allegation of fraud after the defendants had responded to the original suit. Ekwo noted that pre-election cases were sui generis, meaning they belonged to a special category of legal proceedings and were subject to strict timelines. He added that litigants could not institute such actions and subsequently search for evidence to support their claims. The judge also faulted the applicants for failing to challenge claims in the defendants’ counter-affidavits that the proposed amendments were intended to mislead the court. “This is a time-bound suit, and the law makes it mandatory for all exhibits to be filed in court within 14 days of the occurrence of the event being challenged. Anything outside the prescribed 14 days is null and void and of no effect,” the judge held. “I find no merit in this application to bring a fresh exhibit; it is hereby refused for being against the express provision of the law. “I hereby make an order dismissing this application, and it is hereby dismissed,” he ruled. The matter was adjourned until December 2 for hearing. Atiku and the ADC had filed the substantive suit on August 14, seeking an order disqualifying Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election over an allegation that the NYSC discharge certificate submitted by the President to INEC was forged. They also sought an order compelling the electoral commission to remove Tinubu’s name and the APC from the list of candidates and political parties for the election. Following the defendants’ responses, Atiku and the ADC approached the court on September 10, seeking to amend their originating summons. They said the proposed amendments were intended to correct errors in the description of INEC forms attached to their affidavit, provide clearer copies of exhibits, include particulars of the alleged fraud and incorporate Atiku’s written deposition. However, Tinubu opposed the application, arguing that the proposed changes went beyond correcting errors and would introduce new facts, documents and reliefs. He also contended that the original suit was statute-barred and that an incompetent originating process could not be amended. item.title: Many feared dead as overloaded boat capsizes in Bayelsa
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Many passengers are feared dead after a cargo boat conveying more than 300 persons capsized in the riverine area of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday. The ill-fated vessel was reportedly travelling from Anyama Ijaw to Ukubie community when the incident occurred between 12 noon and 1pm. Preliminary reports indicated that the boat, which was allegedly overloaded with passengers travelling to attend a burial ceremony, capsized in the waterways between Oweikorogha and Angiama communities. Eyewitness accounts suggested that the tragedy might have been averted, as some passengers reportedly advised the boat operator to stop at Oweikorogha to reduce the number of persons on board. However, the advice was allegedly ignored, and the boat reportedly capsized shortly after leaving the community. Although the actual casualty figure remained unknown as of the time of filing this report, fears were mounting that the death toll could be high, given the number of passengers on board. The Chairman of the State Maritime Workers Union, Mr Ipigansi Igoniba, confirmed the incident to our correspondent but said details of the disaster were still sketchy. “I cannot give the casualty figure right now. We have sent our members to the scene of the accident, and search and rescue efforts for the missing persons are ongoing,” Igoniba said. Rescue operations were ongoing as efforts continued to establish the number of survivors and fatalities. The incident has thrown the affected communities into mourning and renewed concerns over the dangers of overcrowding and unsafe transportation on Bayelsa’s waterways. item.title: NAFDAC destroys fake, expired drugs, drinks worth N100bn
item.description: …Uncovers illegal cosmetic factory, counterfeit alcohol production hubs in Lagos, Ogun …Mops up 100,000 cartons of banned alcoholic beverages By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) on Friday destroyed fake, counterfeit, expired, banned and substandard drugs, alcoholic beverages, cosmetics and other regulated products worth N100 billion in Ogun State. The destruction exercise, which took place at Ogwama Dumpsite, Ogere Remo, was aimed at preventing dangerous products from re-entering the Nigerian market and endangering public health. Speaking at the flag-off ceremony, the Director-General of NAFDAC, Professor Christiana Mojisola Adeyeye, said the products included counterfeit, expired, controlled, unregistered and banned medicines, as well as unwholesome food products and cosmetics. Among the products destroyed were banned alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and PET bottles below 200ml, banned Analgin injection, expired Codeine cough syrups, Oxytocin injection and counterfeit cosmetics. Adeyeye said: “The estimated street value of these products being destroyed today stands at one hundred billion naira only.” She explained that the exercise was part of the agency’s sustained efforts to prevent expired, fake, substandard and falsified products from finding their way back into circulation. The NAFDAC boss disclosed that recent enforcement operations had exposed several illegal manufacturing and distribution networks, particularly in Lagos and Ogun states. According to her, operatives uncovered a warehouse in Lagos originally meant for tools and hardware, where illegal cosmetic products were being manufactured in the penthouse of the building. She said officers also recovered several cartons of Augmentin and Ampicillin packets, leaflets and other unregistered cosmetics. In another operation, NAFDAC investigators uncovered a production hub where counterfeit versions of popular alcoholic beverage brands were being manufactured, while expired energy drinks were allegedly being revalidated and stored for sale. Adeyeye said suspects arrested in connection with the activities would face the full weight of the law. She further disclosed that NAFDAC officers, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, mopped up more than 100,000 cartons of banned sachet and small PET-bottle alcoholic beverages from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers across Lagos and Ogun states. The agency also uncovered a residential building allegedly converted into a production and distribution centre for unauthorised and registered herbal mixtures being sold in large quantities to Nigerians. Adeyeye said other products destroyed included items seized during enforcement raids and expired products voluntarily surrendered by compliant companies. item.title: Police vow to arrest attackers of Segun Odegbami
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has ordered an immediate investigation into the attack on former Super Eagles captain and sports administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, assuring him that those responsible would be arrested and prosecuted. Ojajuni gave the assurance when he visited Odegbami at his residence in Abeokuta to express the sympathy of the Ogun State Police Command and reassure him of its commitment to protecting lives and property. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists on Friday. During the visit, the commissioner expressed concern over the incident and wished the former football international a speedy recovery, assuring him that the command was treating the matter with the seriousness it deserved. He said he had directed an immediate and comprehensive investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and identify those responsible. Ojajuni also assured Odegbami that the command would deploy all necessary investigative resources to apprehend the suspects and ensure they faced the full weight of the law. The statement partly read: “The Commissioner of Police, Ogun State Command, CP Bode Ojajuni, has paid a visit to former Super Eagles captain and renowned sports administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, to express the Command’s sympathy following the reported incident at his residence in Abeokuta. “The Commissioner conveyed his concern and wished him continued recovery, reaffirming the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state. “CP Ojajuni assured Chief Odegbami that the incident is receiving the Command’s utmost attention. He disclosed that he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, while intensive investigative efforts are ongoing to identify and apprehend those responsible.” The command further confirmed that Odegbami had been discharged from hospital and urged residents to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established police channels. Odegbami, proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM, was reportedly attacked at about 2:30am on Friday at his residence in Ibara GRA, Abeokuta. According to accounts from residents, three armed men allegedly stormed the football legend’s residence and attacked his domestic staff and driver before gaining access to his bedroom. The attackers were said to have inflicted machete cuts on the former footballer during a struggle before fleeing the scene. A resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the assailants initially demanded to know Odegbami’s whereabouts after overpowering members of his domestic staff. item.title: The Other Black Gold: Nigeria’s Coffee Sector Wants A Shot
item.description: Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé. It was not until years later, travelling on the other side of the continent, that Ali had a taste of “coffee, coffee — brewed coffee”. “I have to bring this to Nigeria,” he thought, and he started looking into importing beans from Rwanda. Ali later discovered he did not have to: coffee has been growing in Nigeria for more than 100 years. A wave of entrepreneurs in Africa’s most populous country are turning towards the oil-producing nation’s other black gold — an uphill task in a place full of tea and instant coffee, and little sense of homegrown java as a daily staple or part of a wider cultural patrimony. A general view of someone handling coffee beans in a plantation in the Gorongosa mountain range in Gorongosa on May 20, 2022. (Photo by Alfredo Zuniga / AFP) But roasters say they have found a market — and sense of national pride — to tap into, even if Nigeria’s beans are not well-known. “We need to grow more coffee, whether for the domestic market, which is expanding, or the global market, which is now considering Nigerian coffee,” Ali, founder of Tigray Coffee, which launched in 2021, said over a cup of Nigerian brew, light with slightly chocolatey notes. Agricultural Investments In Ethiopia, hundreds of years of cultivation have bound coffee to local culture, while Uganda and Ivory Coast have become modern export powerhouses. Nigeria produced 1,808 tonnes of beans in 2024, according to statistics from the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation — a paltry sum compared to Kenya’s 49,500 tonnes that same year. The first seeds hit the ground in Nigeria in the 19th century, after coffee was introduced by British colonists. The crop is notoriously fickle and can only grow in certain parts of the country. But there has also been a dearth of investment in agriculture, critics say, as the government instead became over-reliant on the oil sector for revenues. Experts have long called for a more diversified economy. The government agrees, at least in principle: in May, agriculture minister Abubakar Kyari announced federal investments in coffee production in Ondo State, calling it “a powerful economic crop” that could create jobs and “boost rural livelihoods”. ‘Never Imported Coffee’ At the opening of a new cafe in Lagos last month, Princess Adeyinka Tekenah paired a local brew not with croissants, but puff-puff, a staple street food snack of fried dough. “I have been in the business for 12 years, and I have never imported coffee,” the founder of Happy Coffee said. While Tekenah has leaned into her local roots, the coffee industry has also been helped by a growing sense of cosmopolitanism in Nigeria’s cities, Ali said. item.title: Nwifuru reaffirms judicial independence, inaugurates court complex
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru of Ebonyi State has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to judicial independence, stressing the need for an efficient justice system driven by technology and timely dispensation of justice. Nwifuru stated this on Friday at the State High Court, Abakaliki, during the special court session marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year in the state. The governor also inaugurated a Magistrate Court complex comprising six court halls and an exhibit hall, constructed under the administration of the Chief Judge of the state, Justice Elvis Ngene. He advocated the adoption of technology-driven processes in the administration of justice, noting that an efficient justice system must be capable of resolving disputes promptly while minimising unnecessary expenditure of resources. According to him, delays in the administration of justice undermine the effective use of resources, while technological innovations provide opportunities to improve judicial processes and enhance access to justice. “A justice system that cannot resolve disputes timely wastes resources. Technology offers us the opportunity to resolve some of these things. Digital filings and digital transcriptions help. “The significance goes beyond governance. It helps to transact with various registries without recourse to location,” he said. Nwifuru explained that deploying digital technology in judicial administration would reduce the challenges associated with physical processes, improve efficiency and enable legal practitioners and litigants to interact with court registries more conveniently. On judicial independence, the governor described the judiciary as a critical institution for sustaining constitutional democracy and checking possible excesses of the executive arm of government. “An independent judiciary checkmates the government as well as its excesses. As a Governor, I recognise that the independence of the judiciary must be respected and allowed to perform its constitutional and professional mandate,” he stated. He said his administration’s People’s Charter of Needs agenda had prioritised reforms in the justice sector, citing the introduction of electronic filing, establishment of a Moot Court, creation of the Office of the Public Defender and adoption of the Sexual Assault Bill as some of the initiatives. The governor said the measures were aimed at strengthening institutional capacity, promoting access to justice and ensuring that the justice system remained responsive to the needs of the people. Earlier, the Chief Judge of Ebonyi State, Justice Elvis Ngene, said the judiciary had recorded progress in several areas of judicial administration in the last year. He identified the modernisation of judicial processes through technology, protection of judicial integrity, improvement of access to justice and appointment of qualified judicial officers as key areas of focus. item.title: Infantino inspects Warri Stadium, pledges FIFA support during visit
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA President Gianni Infantino has inspected the remodeled Warri City Stadium and pledged the world football body’s continued support for Nigerian football. Infantino visited the Delta State facility on Friday with FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, ahead of its scheduled commissioning on Saturday. He was received at Osubi Airport by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and former Nigeria Football Federation president Amaju Pinnick. Infantino praised the Delta State Government’s investment, saying modern sports facilities could help develop young talent and expand opportunities for boys and girls. He also celebrated Nigeria’s football heritage, highlighting the country’s contribution to the global game. “This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball,” he said, adding that he hoped to return and play there once the remaining work was completed. item.title: Court Rejects Atiku’s Bid To Tender Fresh Evidence In Suit Seeking Tinubu’s Disqualification
item.description: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice President and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to present fresh evidence in his suit seeking to prevent President Bola Tinubu from contesting the 2027 presidential election over allegations of forgery of his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate. The judge held that the time allowed by law to present evidence in a pre-election suit was 14 days, in line with Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution. Justice Ekwo agreed with Tinubu and the other defendants that allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence would alter the nature of the original case and violate the provisions of the Constitution. In his ruling on Atiku’s application to amend the originating summons in the suit against Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the judge held that the former vice president attempted to mislead the court by claiming that the proposed amendment would not introduce fresh issues. Justice Ekwo said that, after carefully examining the application, the court found that the ADC presidential candidate sought to substitute existing evidence with new evidence which, if allowed, would circumvent Section 285(9) of the Constitution, which requires such evidence to be presented within 14 days. A man walks past the Federal High Court premises in Abuja, on April 22, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) According to the judge, allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence through the back door would amount to a fundamental injustice against the defendants. Meanwhile, following an agreement among the lawyers, the judge fixed December 2 for the hearing of the substantive suit. Atiku had told the court that he needed to make substantial amendments to his case challenging Tinubu’s eligibility to participate in the 2027 presidential election. In the main suit, Atiku and the ADC asked Justice Ekwo to disqualify Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election. They challenged the authenticity of Tinubu’s NYSC discharge certificate submitted to INEC by the APC. The plaintiffs, who sued the president, the APC and INEC as the first to third defendants, respectively, in an originating summons marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, alleged that the APC submitted a forged NYSC discharge certificate belonging to the president to INEC. INEC Headquarters in Abuja. They, therefore, asked the court to compel INEC to remove Tinubu’s name and that of the APC from the list of candidates and political parties for the presidential election. However, Tinubu and the APC, in a joint counter-affidavit filed on September 9, urged the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety for being incompetent, arguing that the plaintiffs lacked the legal right to institute the case.
